quote: Cost for - Car, SUV, passenger van - Flat Fee $20 Includes CO surcharge Cost for - Pickup truck, cargo van - Flat Fee (no vertical side planks, top of cab) $37 Includes CO surcharge Cost for - Trailers <1,000 lbs per cubic yard, 2 cubic yard minimum $13.25 per cubic yard + CO surcharge … Unsecured or uncovered loads are subject to double fees at all locations. … The pricing listed is for both Landfills and the Transfer Station.
source_label: Larimer County Solid Waste, 2026 Landfill Fee Schedule
notes: Cloudflare blocks curl. Live page read 2026-09-25 through WebFetch twice (rows and the uncovered-loads line matched), and the same rows were read verbatim in the Wayback capture https://web.archive.org/web/20260310160138/https://www.larimer.gov/solidwaste/fees (that capture's surcharge line is older: live reads 13 cents per car, 25 cents per truck). Any additional weight or volume will incur fees, payable by the resident at the time of disposal. … For details about acceptable items, landfill hours, and other questions, visit: … Vouchers can be picked up at one of the following locations: Greeley Household Hazardous Waste Facility … Dacono Household Hazardous Waste Facility … Weld County Department of Public Health and Environment

There are currently no local locations that can accept it for recycling. … These items can also be posted on Nextdoor, Craigslist, or Facebook Marketplace for others who can make use of them.

notes: Read with curl 2026-09-25. The full A to Z list (https://apps.fcgov.com/recycling/) was searched for turf, synthetic and astro: no entry. Carpet Padding (item 183) says the same about recycling.

fact: California's Department of Toxic Substances Control reports that only 10% of the world's end-of-life artificial turf was recycled in 2021, that even the European Union recycles only 15%, and that in the U.S. demand for turf recycling outpaces capacity.
quote: In 2021, only 10%, or 6.2 million m2 of the world’s end-of-life artificial turf was recycled (Applied Market Information 2022). Even the European Union, the region with the most stringent disposal requirements, recycles only 15% of its volume of artificial turf at the end of life (Applied Market Information 2022). In the U.S., some artificial turf manufacturers have made progress on recycling; however, the demand for recycling outpaces capacity (Applied Market Information 2022).
source_label: California DTSC, Technical Document for Artificial Turf Containing Perfluoroalkyl or Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (Feb. 12, 2026), section 4.3.3 (archived copy, Mar. 26, 2026)
notes: dtsc.ca.gov returns 403 to curl; the PDF was read in full from the Wayback capture of 2026-03-26 with pdftotext on 2026-09-25. The next sentence says there are no artificial turf recycling facilities in California.

fact: California's DTSC says recycling the blades and backing of worn-out artificial turf has historically been rare, that reusing the infill is more common, that newer turf recycling programs often burn or shred the turf, and that landfill is the most common end.
quote: Historically, recycling of the blades and backing of end-of-life artificial turf has been rare (The Intercept 2019); reuse of infill material (which is outside the scope of the current document) is more common (Zandwijk RTS 2022). Although turf recycling programs have emerged in recent years, they often require the burning or shredding of end-of-life artificial turf, which may lead to worker exposure and continued consumer exposure to PFASs (Ismawati et al. 2023; TenCate 2020). Artificial turf is most commonly disposed of in landfills after its intended use (Berger 2016).
source_label: California DTSC, Technical Document for Artificial Turf Containing Perfluoroalkyl or Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (Feb. 12, 2026), section 5.3 (archived copy, Mar. 26, 2026)
notes: Read from the Wayback capture with pdftotext on 2026-09-25 (dtsc.ca.gov blocks curl).

fact: California's DTSC calls incinerating used artificial turf problematic because the fluoropolymers in turf blades can form toxic combustion products.
quote: Incineration, which is another potential way to dispose of used artificial turf, is problematic because the fluoropolymers in artificial turf blades can form toxic combustion products (e.g., perchlorofluoroalkanoic acids and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons)
source_label: California DTSC, Technical Document for Artificial Turf Containing Perfluoroalkyl or Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (Feb. 12, 2026), section 5.3 (archived copy, Mar. 26, 2026)
notes: Read from the Wayback capture with pdftotext on 2026-09-25. The document's concern is fluoropolymer PFAS used as processing aids in turf fibers.

fact: California's DTSC says turf can legally go to any California landfill that accepts municipal solid waste, but that landfills often refuse large amounts of it because of its bulk.
quote: Artificial turf can be legally disposed of in any landfill in California that accepts municipal solid waste. However, due to its bulk, landfills often refuse to accept large amounts of artificial turf; this can lead to artificial turf being stored elsewhere under unsuitable conditions (Lundstrom et al. 2019).
source_label: California DTSC, Technical Document for Artificial Turf Containing Perfluoroalkyl or Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (Feb. 12, 2026), section 4.3.3 (archived copy, Mar. 26, 2026)
notes: California practice, cited for why a Northern Colorado hauler should call the gate first; no Colorado site we read refuses turf in writing.

fact: FairWarning reported in 2019 that the technology to separate turf's plastic grass and backing from its sand and rubber infill still wasn't fully developed in the United States, or was deemed too expensive.
quote: But the technology to recycle this complex product – separating the plastic grass and backing from the sand and rubber infill – still isn’t fully developed in the United States, or is deemed too expensive, according to one industry report and interviews with turf experts.
source_label: FairWarning, Fields of Waste (published by Investigate Midwest, Dec. 19, 2019)
notes: Read in full with curl on 2026-09-25. The article is about sports fields.

fact: FairWarning reported that a niche trade reclaims old field turf and sells pieces to homeowners for landscaping, batting cages and dog kennels, and that eventually those pieces are bound for the dumpster too.

source_label: FairWarning, Fields of Waste (published by Investigate Midwest, Dec. 19, 2019)

fact: The Colorado Sun reported in October 2023 that Fort Collins and other cities were studying bans on installing artificial turf, and listed a lack of recycling options for old artificial grass among the concerns.
quote: Fort Collins and other cities are also studying bans on installation of artificial, plastic grass as a turf replacement, Rogers said. Artificial turf comes with increasing concerns about PFAS “forever chemicals” used in manufacturing and then shedding in water runoff, as well as creating urban heat islands and a lack of recycling options for old artificial grass.
source_label: The Colorado Sun, Colorado cities accelerate turf wars with new construction bans, public median rip-outs (Michael Booth, Oct. 10, 2023)
notes: Read with curl 2026-09-25. Rogers is a Western Resource Advocates staffer; the concern list is the reporter's paraphrase, not a Fort Collins statement. Fort Collins' current turf rules are in city-codes.json (fc-luc-5.10.1).

fact: Motz's Envirofill installation chart pairs a 1.5 to 1.75 inch landscape pile with 1/2 to 3/4 inch of infill at 2.5 to 3.5 pounds per square foot.
quote: The following chart provides depth and quantity ratios. … 12/20 or 16/30 1½-1 ¾” (38-44mm) Landscape ½” – ¾” (13-19mm) 2.5-3.5lbs (12.21-17.09kg/m2)
source_label: The Motz Group, Envirofill Installation Guidelines: Landscape & Recreational Applications (PDF)
notes: Read with curl and pdftotext 2026-09-25. Fractions 1½ and 1¾ inch are written 1.5 and 1.75 in the fact. One maker's rate for its own product; other infills and makers differ.

fact: MSI says total weight is turf's weight in ounces per square yard including the backing (and infill, if applicable), and that its Evergrass Viridian Turf 91 has a 65-ounce face weight inside a 91-ounce total, 26 ounces of it backing.
quote: For turf, total weight refers to how much it weighs in ounces per square yard. This measurement includes both the face weight and the backing material, as well as the infill, if applicable. … Evergrass ™ Viridian Turf 91 has a face weight of 65 oz/sq yd, but its total weight of 91 oz accounts for 26 oz of backing material
source_label: MSI Surfaces, Understanding Pile Height, Face Weight, and Total Weight (blog, July 12, 2023)
notes: Read with curl 2026-09-25. The 91-ounce total is the turf as sold, before infill.

fact: Arithmetic on two published specs, not a weighed yard: a 500-square-foot lawn of 91-ounce turf weighs about 316 pounds (91 ÷ 9 ÷ 16 = about 0.63 pounds a square foot), its infill at Motz's 2.5 to 3.5 pounds a square foot weighs 1,250 to 1,750 pounds, the two together about 1,566 to 2,066 pounds against a one-ton (2,000-pound) load limit, and the infill runs about 4 to 5.5 times the turf's weight.
source_label: Worked example on the Motz Envirofill chart and MSI's Viridian Turf 91 total weight
notes: The quote is the Motz chart row the arithmetic starts from; the 91-ounce total weight is MSI's (how-to-dispose-of-artificial-turf.msi-viridian-91-total-weight). 91 oz/sq yd ÷ 9 = 10.11 oz/sq ft = 0.632 lb/sq ft; × 500 = 316 lb. 2.5 × 500 = 1,250 lb; 3.5 × 500 = 1,750 lb. 316 + 1,250 = 1,566; 316 + 1,750 = 2,066. 2.5 ÷ 0.632 = 3.96; 3.5 ÷ 0.632 = 5.54. One short ton = 2,000 lb.

fact: Integriturf's installation guide says most turf rolls are made 15 feet wide by 100 feet long, and that the most common way to secure turf is nailing every 4 to 6 inches around the perimeter and every 2 to 3 feet on center across the field with 5-inch or 6-inch nails.
quote: Most manufacturers produce their rolls in 15ft widths and 100ft lengths (a full roll = 15 x 100ft or 1,500 square feet). … 6. Securing the turf: The most common method of securing the turf is to nail the turf every 4 to 6 inches around the perimeter and every 2 to 3 feet on center throughout the field using either 5-inch 40D Common, or, 6-inch electro-galvanized nails.
notes: Read with curl and pdftotext 2026-09-25. One installer's guide describing installation; the page uses it only to say how many fasteners an old lawn may hold.
